family.description: This domain is a CTP-dependent riboflavin kinase (RFK), found in archaea, that catalyses the phosphorylation of riboflavin to form flavin mononucleotide in riboflavin biosynthesis [ec:2.7.1.26]. Its structure resembles a RIFT barrel, structurally similar to but topologically distinct from bacterial and eukaryotic examples. The N-terminal is a winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain, and the C-terminal half is most similar in sequence to a group of cradle-loop barrels. [swissprot:O28174] has this domain attached to [pfam:PF00325].
family.name: Domain of unknown function DUF120

record.description: This domain is a CTP-dependent riboflavin kinase (RFK), found in archaea, that catalyses the phosphorylation of riboflavin to form flavin mononucleotide in riboflavin biosynthesis [ec:2.7.1.26]. Its structure resembles a RIFT barrel, structurally similar to but topologically distinct from bacterial and eukaryotic examples. The N-terminal is a winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain, and the C-terminal half is most similar in sequence to a group of cradle-loop barrels. [swissprot:O28174] has this domain attached to [pfam:PF00325].

evidence.explanation: Equal-concentration ATP/GTP yield 30%/11% of CTP activity; no-added-metal protein contains 4-5 mol Mg per mol protein.
Abstract inspected but original full text returned 403; IUBMB cites this study for lack of ATP/GTP use.
Ammelburg's 2011 primary account supplies the original assay protocol and qualitative donor contrasts; Figure9G retains a small FMN-labeled ATP peak despite its negative caption.

discussions.notes: The 2011 dissertation is a primary account of the 2007 work, not independent replication or verified journal-text identity. Its assay contains 5 mM MgCl2 without a metal-removal intervention. Different constructs and assay conditions do not establish why 2008 ATP/GTP activity differs. Original journal text and donor-purity/metal controls remain follow-ups. EC2.7.1.161 is current nomenclature; the frozen EC2.7.1.26 description remains imported source text, not curated chemistry.
discussions.prompt: Resolve nucleotide-donor and metal dependence across the original RibK studies.
discussions.rationale: The 2008 enzyme retains ATP/GTP activity and copurified Mg; strict CTP-only and metal-independent claims are not justified by these assays.

evidence.explanation: Whole-fusion biochemical assays and DNA-bound structure support distinct observations; activation and FMN-induced structural switching remain proposed.
Static apo and product complexes motivate an explicitly hypothetical ordered-binding and E107 base model; no causal residue intervention was inspected.

discussions.notes: Archived A0A0K1E2F9 entry33 maps AKT35049.1 to PF01982 at 88-208; the current entry is deleted. Q60365 sequence2 postdates the original studies. The 136-aa archived Q60365 and 2P3M/2VBU/2VBV references have an MVKL prefix relative to current 132-aa Q60365; deposited E107 maps to current E103 and PF01982 7-125 maps to deposited 11-129. The prefix is not established as a vector tag. Verify physical inserts, cleavage junctions, folding/abundance and residue perturbations before stronger transfer.
discussions.prompt: Resolve exact constructs, causal residue roles and native regulatory polarity without assigning wHTH activity to PF01982 alone.
discussions.rationale: Reference-domain annotations and static contacts do not establish domain sufficiency, proton transfer or native transcriptional activation.

evidence.explanation: Figure4 and supplement S3/TableS3 were visually inspected; myRbkR text nanomolar affinity differs from plotted micromolar titrations, and EMSA length is 104 versus 102 bp.

discussions.notes: Preserve 4D's 15 nM DNA versus general Methods 10 nM and TableS3's py probe ordering. No numerical correction or replicate refit. Ammelburg2011 Methods and Figures9/11/12 are now inspected, with an ATP panel/caption discrepancy and printed preparation-volume ambiguity retained. Original 2007 journal text, remaining supplements and later experiments are still gaps. Gene adjacency and predicted regulons are not causal proof.
